topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture’s purpose of bringing previously studied immune components together to explain inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how innate immune cells distinguish danger through molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how TLR engagement produces immune responses tailored to the location and nature of the detected threat.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition pathways and inflammatory disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how recognition pathways beyond TLRs convert microbial or damage signals into inflammation that can contribute to disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells initiate inflammatory signals that bring circulating leukocytes to the infection site.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how infection information leaves the affected tissue through lymphatic drainage to initiate adaptive responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity subsides through the loss of activating stimuli and the action of inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the tissue-level outcomes of inflammation when complete restoration of homeostasis is difficult.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next session.
